learning: Iteration 9 reproduced iteration 7 exactly, so the geometry is a stable base. The s-bend oscillation (0.317) is the open controller question. Bend max_error has stayed on its plateau under every geometry change, so the next test is controller-side damping, and the lead test comes only after the controller is stable.
notes: Iteration 7 geometry held exactly as the Builder asked. Only kd changes (0.375 to 0.33) to test whether damping the s-bend oscillation of 0.317 brings it under the 0.3 threshold while oval progress holds.
rationale: The Builder's geometry reproduces iteration 7 exactly: 50 mm span at 12.5 mm pitch, 12 mm footprints, y 0.05 lead, wheel_track 0.10 m. Iteration 9 already raced this geometry with the iteration 7 controller and returned the same score (399.74, oval progress 0.995, 20 of 20 oval finishes). That makes a controller-only change the one informative test this iteration. The only controller metric outside the plateau is s-bend steering_oscillation at 0.317, above the 0.3 threshold the Builder asked about. Bend max_error (s-bend 0.0676 m, slalom 0.0608 m) and line losses (about 1 per run) show that sensing holds the tape and that the excursions are turn-induced. Oval progress holds with a wide margin, so I lower kd from 0.375 to 0.33 (about 12 percent) to damp the derivative response that drives the jitter. kp 3.75 and ki 0.21 stay unchanged so the effect on oscillation is attributable. Expected result: s-bend steering_oscillation at or below 0.3 and oval progress at or above 0.95. The main risk is a small rise in bend max_error, because less damping can allow more overshoot on the s-bend. If oscillation falls but oval progress drops below 0.95, I would restore kd 0.375 next iteration.
